title: RRDA edit and suppress roles with shared Mirror-conditioned adapter
hypothesis: One shared physical adapter basis plus role coordinates represents edit and suppress functions with less edit-state bytes when role updates align; increasing role angle reveals when a second/private basis is required.
routing: Role label/router is identical and charged for every method; this experiment isolates adapter state and function, not routing quality.
storage: Actual serialized .npz inference payload includes base executor, router/role IDs, basis, codes, metadata and all reconstruction state. Report full bytes and role-adapter-state bytes separately.
success_gate: At angle 0 on both seeds: role errors <=1e-5 and shared rank1 role-state <=75% of independent adapters. Across angles, rank2 should restore <=1e-5 if rank1 fails. Mirror-specific success additionally requires strict gain over native role gate/lowrank control.
failure_gate: No edit-state storage gain at aligned angle, role quality miss, or exact native gate/basis alias. Fresh sealed after any failure.
boundaries: Base payload charged and separately reported
